headline: Southeast Asia Achieves Major Disease Elimination Milestones
meta_description: Timor Leste, Bhutan, and Thailand celebrate WHO-recognized health victories with elimination of trachoma, dog-mediated rabies, and rubella.
summary_short: Three Southeast Asian nations have achieved major public health milestones, eliminating diseases that once caused widespread suffering across the region.
body:
The World Health Organization has recognized major disease elimination victories across Southeast Asia, marking turning points in public health for three nations. Timor Leste has eliminated trachoma, Bhutan has eliminated dog-mediated human rabies, and Thailand has eliminated rubella—achievements that reflect decades of sustained effort and regional cooperation.

Each victory represents a different challenge overcome. Trachoma, once a leading infectious cause of blindness, is gone from Timor Leste. Bhutan's success against dog-mediated rabies required controlling disease transmission at its source. Thailand's rubella elimination protects future generations from a virus that can cause severe birth defects.

These successes underscore what focused public health initiatives can accomplish. Bangladesh, meanwhile, has beaten its 2030 targets ahead of schedule, suggesting the momentum for disease elimination is accelerating across the region. Together, these wins demonstrate that with coordination and commitment, even diseases considered intractable can be defeated.
quick_facts: Timor Leste eliminated trachoma, a leading infectious cause of blindness
Bhutan eliminated dog-mediated human rabies transmission
Thailand eliminated rubella, preventing birth defects
Bangladesh beat its 2030 health targets early
WHO recognized all major achievements across Southeast Asia
